name: IEC dynamic input with negation (falling edge)
summary: Clock wedge combined with a negation circle or polarity triangle, so the input acts on a falling edge.
description: Combining the dynamic input wedge with input negation, or with a polarity indicator, means the input is active on the transition from high to low. TI's public overview tabulates how the active transition reads in positive logic, negative logic and polarity notation.

Negative-edge clocking appears in JK flip-flops and some counters, and in designs where two stages are clocked on opposite edges. A reader must check both the wedge and the external mark before deciding which edge the device responds to.

The symbol does not state duty-cycle or minimum pulse width requirements; those come from device timing data. The input waveform must satisfy those limits at the active falling transition, not just reach a valid steady logic level.
readingNotes: Look outside the outline for the circle or triangle as well as inside for the wedge.
Opposite-edge clocking between stages is often deliberate.
drawingChecklist: Draw both the wedge and the external negation mark.
Keep notation consistent with the rest of the sheet.
Annotate the clock net with its active edge if mixed edges are used.
distinction: A wedge without an external mark is rising-edge triggered.
